messages.content:
How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
version:3.1.0
IP:192.168.11.33
API name: get nodes list
Parameter_fabricName:PEK-ACI

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve a list of nodes associated with a specified fabric in a network. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to send the GET request to. The URL should include the target IP, API endpoint, and the fabricName query parameter placeholder https://<ip>/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName={fabricName}.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric whose nodes are to be listed. This value is used to replace the {fabricName} placeholder in the URL.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?" They provide version, IP, API name, Parameter_fabricName. They want to generate a RESTful API request. We have a tool function requests_get that can send an HTTP GET request. The function signature expects url (optional) and fabricName. The default URL includes placeholder. We need to call the function with the correct URL replacing <ip> with 192.168.11.33 and fabricName with PEK-ACI.

We should produce a JSON response with the result from the function. According to guidelines, we should not reveal internal details. But we can show the output of the function. So we will call the function with url: "https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI" and fabricName: "PEK-ACI". Then we return the result as JSON. That is the expected behavior.
